{"id": "989aa5bf-31c3-4725-acbf-b3a15564e87d", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_gHTZ0CvedmNm5HaqpV1S3n", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Scaling and throughput best practices\",\"context\":\"## `bedrock-mantle` endpoint: throughput and quotas\\n\\nThe `bedrock-mantle` endpoint has the following quota behavior:\\n\\n* Models with published quotas have separate per-model, per-Region input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas.\\n* The endpoint does not enforce RPM quotas. Two workloads with the same RPM can consume very different amounts of capacity, so plan and rate-limit by tokens and concurrency instead of RPM alone.\\n* When a request is admitted, the input-token check includes the input tokens plus the requested `max_tokens` value. After the response completes, the unused part of that reservation is replenished. Set `max_tokens` no higher than your application needs.\\n* Models without published TPM quotas do not currently have per-account TPM quotas exposed in Service Quotas. This does not mean that throughput is unlimited; internal service capacity and transient rate limiting still apply.\\n* Batch inference and Provisioned Throughput are available only through `bedrock-runtime`. Service-tier and model support varies by model.\\n\\nDefault values and your account's allocations can vary by model, Region, and usage history. For current values, quota evaluation details, and the AWS Support process for requesting an increase, see Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint. See the applicable Models at a glance for model-specific endpoint, service-tier, and feature support\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Quotas for Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"# Quotas for Amazon Bedrock\\n\\nYour AWS account has default quotas, formerly referred to as limits, for Amazon Bedrock. To view\\nservice quotas for Amazon Bedrock, do one of the following:\\n\\n* Follow the steps at Viewing service\\n quotas and select **Amazon Bedrock** as the service.\\n* Refer to the Amazon Bedrock service quotas in the AWS General Reference.\\n\\nModel inference in Amazon Bedrock is controlled by quotas on token usage. Some models use tokens at a higher rate. For more information about these rates and how to optimize your token usage, see How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock.\\n\\nEmbedding models are an exception: they are throttled by requests per minute (RPM) rather than tokens per minute (TPM). Use the RPM quota when you plan capacity or request a quota increase for an embedding model. For more information, see Amazon Titan Text Embeddings models.\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock offers two inference endpoints \u2013 `bedrock-runtime` and `bedrock-mantle` \u2013 each with its own per-model quota allocations. Traffic to the two endpoints is tracked against separate quotas, even when calling the same underlying model. For details, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint and Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint.\\n\\nTo maintain the performance of the service and to ensure appropriate usage of Amazon Bedrock, the\\ndefault quotas assigned to an account might be updated depending on regional factors,\\naccount age, usage history, payment history, fraudulent usage, and/or approval of a quota increase request.\\nAs a result, the quotas that apply to your account might be lower than the default values\\nlisted in the Amazon Bedrock service quotas. To check the values that apply to your account, use Service Quotas as\\ndescribed earlier in this topic.\\n\\nQuota increases aren't granted automatically. For the request process and the conditions\\nthat apply to a request, see Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas.\\n\\n###### Topics\\n\\n* How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock\\n* Monitor your token usage by counting tokens before running inference\\n* Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\\n* Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\\n* Request an increase for Amazon Bedrock quotas\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Accessing OpenAI GPT models on Amazon Bedrock with global cross-Region inference in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Taiwan | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Quota management\\n\\nGPT-6 quotas on `bedrock-runtime` are measured in tokens per minute (TPM), tracked against the source Region you call from. Input and cache-write tokens count 1:1, and each output token consumes 10 tokens of quota. For example, a request with 2,000 input tokens and 1,000 output tokens depletes 12,000 tokens from your quota.\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock reserves the full `max_tokens` up front, so set it close to the completions you expect. One quota covers `InvokeModel`, Converse, Responses, and Chat Completions. Review and raise it on the Service Quotas console from your source Region. Before production, request increases early and alarm on `EstimatedTPMQuotaUsage` in the `AWS/Bedrock` namespace at 70\u201380 percent of your allocation. See How tokens are counted in Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock endpoints and quotas for current values\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/accessing-openai-gpt-models-on-amazon-bedrock-with-global-cross-region-inference-in-thailand-malaysia-singapore-indonesia-and-taiwan/\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Global cross-Region inference for latest Anthropic Claude Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models on Amazon Bedrock in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Taiwan | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"### Understanding quotas and planning for scale\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock enforces service quotas to support fair resource allocation and system stability. For Global CRIS, quotas are measured in two dimensions, each serving a distinct purpose in capacity management:\\n\\n* **Tokens per minute (TPM)** \u2013 The maximum number of tokens (input + output) that can be processed per minute.\\n* **Requests per minute (RPM)** \u2013 The maximum number of inference requests that can be made per minute.\\n\\nDefault quotas vary by model and are allocated per source Region. You can view your current quotas in the AWS Service Quotas console by navigating to Amazon Bedrock service quotas in your source Region (Singapore or Jakarta).\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock uses a token burndown rate that weighs output tokens more heavily than input tokens when calculating quota consumption. The burndown rate is 5:1, meaning output tokens consume five times more quota than input tokens because generating tokens requires more computation than processing input.\\n\\n`Quota consumption = Input tokens + (Output tokens \u00d7 5)`\\n\\nFor example, if your request uses 10,000 input tokens and generates 5,000 output tokens:\\n\\n`Total quota consumption = 10,000 + (5,000 \u00d7 5) = 35,000 tokens`\\n\\nThe request consumes 35,000 tokens against your TPM quota for throttling purposes. When planning capacity requirements and requesting quota increases, you need to account for this burndown rate in your calculations. If your application processes requests with this same token pattern at 100 requests per minute, the total quota consumption would be 3,500,000 TPM (100 requests \u00d7 35,000 tokens per request). When working with your AWS Account Manager on quota increase requests, provide your expected request volume, average input tokens per request, and average output tokens per request so they can calculate the appropriate quota allocation using this burndown multiplier\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/global-cross-region-inference-for-latest-anthropic-claude-opus-sonnet-and-haiku-models-on-amazon-bedrock-in-thailand-malaysia-singapore-indonesia-and-taiwan/\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search Bedrock docs for bedrock-mantle endpoint quotas and usage types"}

{"id": "4244ed83-8ba1-47e9-a5c1-089fd5afb545", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_kA7jNU2kFPLKm9ukERQLdD", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Inference endpoints supported by Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"# Inference endpoints supported by Amazon Bedrock\\n\\nAn endpoint is the URL that your application uses to send inference requests to Amazon Bedrock. Amazon Bedrock provides two inference endpoints. The endpoint you choose determines which APIs and features are available.\\n\\nFor most new applications, use the `bedrock-runtime` endpoint. Use `bedrock-mantle` when you specifically need capabilities that are currently available only there, such as server-side and pre-configured tools (including web search), background inference, Projects, or Workspaces. To see which endpoint each model supports, see Endpoint availability. The following table compares the two endpoints.\\n\\n| **Endpoint** | **Supported APIs** | **Description** |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com` (recommended) | InvokeModel / Converse / Chat Completions / Responses API / Messages API | Region-specific endpoints for making inference requests for models hosted in Amazon Bedrock using the InvokeModel/Converse/Chat Completions/Responses/Messages APIs. For more information about the Bedrock-native operations, see Amazon Bedrock Runtime API operations. The OpenAI-compatible APIs are called on the `/openai/v1` paths of this endpoint rather than through the AWS SDKs. |\\n| `bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws` | Responses API / Chat Completions API / Messages API | Region-specific endpoints for making inference requests for models hosted in Amazon Bedrock using the OpenAI-compatible endpoints and the Anthropic Messages API. |\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nBoth endpoints use the same underlying Mantle inference engine. The `bedrock-mantle` name identifies an endpoint surface, not a different inference engine.\\n\\nExisting applications that use `bedrock-mantle` continue to be fully supported and do not need to change. Both endpoints let you bring an existing OpenAI SDK codebase to Amazon Bedrock by changing only the base URL and API key, and both support the OpenAI-compatible Responses and Chat Completions APIs and the Anthropic Messages API.\\n\\nAPI support\\n\\n| API | `bedrock-runtime` | `bedrock-mantle` |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| InvokeModel | | |\\n| Converse / ConverseStream | | |\\n| Chat Completions (OpenAI-compatible) | | |\\n| Responses API (OpenAI-compatible) | | |\\n| Messages API (Anthropic-native) |\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/endpoints.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Responses API\",\"context\":\"# Responses API\\n\\nAmazon Bedrock provides the OpenAI Responses API on both the `bedrock-runtime` and\\n`bedrock-mantle` endpoints. Use `bedrock-runtime` for new\\napplications. Use `bedrock-mantle` only when a model or capability that you\\nrequire isn't available on `bedrock-runtime`.\\n\\n| **Endpoint** | **Base URL** | **When to use** |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| `bedrock-runtime` (recommended) | `https://bedrock-runtime.{region}.amazonaws.com/openai/v1` | New applications and migrations when the required model and Responses API features are supported. |\\n| `bedrock-mantle` (compatibility) | `https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/v1` | Existing applications and workloads that require Mantle-only support, such as Responses API access to GPT OSS models, background inference, or server-side tools. |\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nOn `bedrock-mantle`, the path prefix varies by model. Most models are served\\nunder `/v1`, as shown in the preceding table, but some are served under\\n`/openai/v1` instead. A request that uses the wrong prefix for a model is\\nrejected with `model `<model-id>` isn't supported on this\\nroute`. To confirm the base URL for a specific model, see the\\n**Programmatic Access** table on its card in\\nModels at a glance.\\n\\nThe two endpoints don't have identical feature support. Requests on\\n`bedrock-runtime` are always synchronous, server-side tools aren't available, and\\nonly the default project is supported. For the full comparison, see Inference endpoints supported by Amazon Bedrock,\\nand for the details of each difference, see Using the Responses API on the bedrock-runtime endpoint.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nWhen using the OpenAI SDK with Amazon Bedrock, you must point it to the Amazon Bedrock endpoint, not the OpenAI endpoint. Set the following environment variables, choosing the base URL for the endpoint you want:\\n\\n```\\n# bedrock-runtime (recommended)\\nOPENAI_BASE_URL=\\\"https://bedrock-runtime.<your-region>.amazonaws.com/openai/v1\\\"\\n\\n# bedrock-mantle\\nOPENAI_BASE_URL=\\\"https://bedrock-mantle.<your-region>.api.aws/v1\\\"\\n\\nOPENAI_API_KEY=\\\"<your Bedrock API key>\\\"\\n```\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/inference-responses-api.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Gemma 4 31B\",\"context\":\"## Programmatic Access\\n\\nUse the following model IDs and endpoint URLs to access this model programmatically. For more information about the available APIs and endpoints, see APIs supported and Endpoints supported.\\n\\n| **Endpoint** | **Model ID** | **In-Region endpoint URL** | **Geo inference ID** | **Global inference ID** |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n| `bedrock-mantle` | `google.gemma-4-31b` | `https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/openai/v1` | Not supported | Not supported |\\n\\n*For example, if region is us-east-1 (N. Virginia), then the bedrock-mantle endpoint URL will be \\\"https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/openai/v1\\\".*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-google-gemma-4-31b.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"gpt-oss-120b\",\"context\":\"## Programmatic Access\\n\\nUse the following model IDs and endpoint URLs to access this model programmatically. Virginia), then the bedrock-runtime endpoint URL will be \\\"https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com\\\" and for bedrock-mantle will be \\\"https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/v1\\\".*\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-card-openai-gpt-oss-120b.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"GPT-5.5\",\"context\":\"## Programmatic Access\\n\\nUse the following model IDs and endpoint URLs to access this model programmatically. {"id": "bd75eea8-cf52-4d1a-8220-be757454812d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Probably, but the usage type name alone doesn't prove it.** I'd confirm it from your own traffic before relying on that quota.

**What the docs say**
- Bedrock has two inference endpoints, `bedrock-runtime` and `bedrock-mantle`. Their quotas are tracked separately, even for the same model.
- The docs say both endpoints "use the same underlying Mantle inference engine". They also say the `bedrock-mantle` name "identifies an endpoint surface, not a different inference engine."
- The Cost and Usage Report docs list `*-mantle-input-tokens-*` as a usage type pattern for input tokens. They don't say that usage type is billed only for calls to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint.
- The Mantle engine can serve some models on `bedrock-runtime` too. So "mantle" in the line item could mean the engine rather than the endpoint you call. I couldn't find a doc that settles this either way.

**What's solid**
- The quota that applies depends on which endpoint your clients call. The usage type doesn't decide it.
- If you call `bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws`, the per-model `bedrock-mantle` input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas apply. Those are separate quotas, not one combined number.
- If you call `bedrock-runtime`, the runtime TPM quota applies instead. It counts input and output tokens together against one per-model quota.
- On `bedrock-mantle`, each request is checked against input tokens plus `max_tokens`, and the unused part is returned afterward. A large `max_tokens` can cause 429s even when your real input is small.

1. Check the base URL or SDK config in your client code. A host of `bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws` means the mantle quotas apply. A host of `bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com` means the runtime quota applies.
